scope: Registered-donor coordination with normal 10/25/50 km then all-coverage alerts, immediate emergency broadcast, donor slots/waiting replacements, private coordinator checks and compressed hospital-proof uploads; private admin-visible checkbox responses and dialler-based validation; no blood-stock or hospital medical-record functionality.

workflow.execution: Work on any feature whose dependsOn entries are done. Order is a suggested roadmap, not a blocking chain. Independent ready features may proceed in parallel.
workflow.projectCompleteWhen: All 45 features are done and final handoff is accepted.
workflow.parallelTagMeaning: A feature tagged parallel does not depend on the immediately preceding feature; it may start alongside other ready features once all listed prerequisites are done.

features.title: Project plan and scope
acceptanceCriteria: Plan covers architecture, roles, pilot boundaries, two-stage checking, delivery stages, and completion gates.
Blood-stock functionality is explicitly excluded.

features.title: Local development toolchain
acceptanceCriteria: Clean checkout installs pinned dependencies and starts/stops local services through documented commands.
Commands fail clearly for missing prerequisites and never reset a remote database.

Node/web pnpm workspaces, pinned Flutter/Dart SDK with pub lockfile, Docker Compose PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Express/worker, Next.js and Flutter command wrappers replace previous-stack declarations; missing packages fail clearly.
Documented local startup and clean-checkout checks include Prisma tooling, TypeScript checks, flutter analyze and Flutter tests; no TypeScript mobile workspace or Supabase runtime is required.
Pin pnpm 10.32.1 and Node 24; replace old Supabase/Hono dependencies, apps/* workspace/env/typecheck paths and TypeScript-mobile scripts with backend/admin/packages and Flutter SDK commands.

Implement actual runner/secret checks, Compose health/start/stop/local reset and lockfiles; record Docker/registry failures as blockers. Explicit-path reviewed baseline excludes unrelated legacy deletions and reproduces in a clean checkout.
evidence: docs/progress.md: 2026-10-02 F002 parallel toolchain implementation and clean-checkout verification (partial; remote baseline push blocked)

features.title: Database foundation
acceptanceCriteria: PostgreSQL 17, PostGIS, extensions, migrations, indexes, and grants apply from an empty local database.
A clean reset reproduces the schema and synthetic seeds.

Prisma schema, PostgreSQL adapter, migrations and synthetic seed are the single database deployment path; reviewed SQL preserves spatial indexes, workflow functions, constraints and least-privilege grants/RLS.

Previous supabase migration drafts are ported and tested without Supabase Auth roles/auth.uid/JWT or PGMQ/Cron dependencies; backend identity/session tables and durable outbox/job tables reconstruct from an empty database.
Foundation scope is backend identity/session and organization/membership infrastructure; F004 owns donor/request workflow tables. New schemas/seeds use canonical urgency rather than old SQL values.

features.title: Private workflow data model
acceptanceCriteria: Requests, pledges, initial checks, hospital outcomes, certificates, audit, idempotency, and jobs have tested constraints.
Only approved bounded preliminary questionnaire responses are stored privately; no weights, diagnoses, detailed histories or test values. Private donor/assigned-staff access and redaction are tested.

Versioned coverage, urgency response/contact/offer windows, v1 outstanding-unit slot target and confirmed-coverage policy, search/evaluation state, expansion audit and unique original invitations have tested constraints.

Slot reservations, waiting pledges, expiring replacement offers, questionnaire versions/private responses/sharing consent and proof-upload states have concurrency/uniqueness constraints; responses never appear in public/requester/notification views.
Request origin REQUESTER/STAFF separates creator, requesting contact and coordinator; urgency is NORMAL/URGENT/CRITICAL/EMERGENCY, with typed API/client parity.
Contact versions/validation, independent hospital hold flag, paused coordination deadlines and consent-withdrawal slot release follow plan transition contracts.

features.title: Organization and staff authorization
acceptanceCriteria: Verified hospitals, NSS partnerships, memberships, and MFA scope every staff action.
Unassigned, revoked, non-MFA, and self-verifying donors are denied at API and database boundaries.
Trusted backend actor/MFA context and least-privilege database roles prevent callers from choosing another identity or bypassing scoped SQL/RLS.

Either authorized hospital staff or NSS coordinator may publish assigned requests without a mandatory second publisher; assigned admins can create/edit/activate questionnaire versions under hospital-approved policy with audit.

features.title: Authentication and account lifecycle
acceptanceCriteria: Verified email/password, Google, iOS Apple sign-in, recovery, refresh, logout, and disable work.
Staff TOTP and sensitive-change reauthentication pass integration tests.
Email/password registration and supported provider sign-in create or resume one account/profile; verification and repeat registration cannot bypass activation or duplicate profiles.

Express-owned identity uses bcrypt hashes, expiring single-use verification/reset tokens, short-lived JWT access and hashed rotating refresh sessions; replay, logout, disable and linked provider ownership checks pass.
Backend auth API and session/provider tests run without requiring later Flutter/web clients; F008 owns browser session transport and F009 owns mobile credential/refresh integration.

features.title: API foundation and contracts
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned Node.js/Express/TypeScript API uses router/schema/service modules, Zod validation, OpenAPI, TypeScript/Dart contracts, health and consistent errors.
Invalid input, expired sessions, and internal-error redaction are tested.

features.title: Next.js browser session integration
acceptanceCriteria: Secure HTTP-only cookies, CSRF/origin checks, refresh, and logout work.
Tokens are not exposed to browser JavaScript and cross-origin tests pass.

Next.js server runtime on Vercel proxies authenticated Express calls using server-held credentials; Axios/browser flows use protected same-origin session routes without storing backend tokens in Zustand or browser storage.

features.title: Web and Flutter client foundations
acceptanceCriteria: OpenAPI schemas, language keys/copy and design tokens serve TypeScript web and Dart mobile through platform-specific clients/forms; generated models and locale parity checks prevent drift.
Offline/retry behavior never reports an unconfirmed mutation as successful.
Flutter uses feature-based screens/providers/repositories, Riverpod, Dio, GoRouter, secure storage and localization/ARB; Next.js uses TanStack Query, Zustand, Axios and i18next.
Flutter unit/widget tests and web tests verify shared API/locale contracts without assuming Dart imports TypeScript or React components.
Flutter secure storage/Dio refresh and typed generated models integrate with completed backend identity; web tokens remain confined to F008 server session routes.

features.title: Verified hospital directory
acceptanceCriteria: Administrators verify hospitals and publish safe contact, location, and staffed-hour details.
Only verified, non-held hospitals can accept new requests.

features.title: Request submission
acceptanceCriteria: Requester can select an actual hospital and draft, submit, edit, cancel, or correct a request.
Private references and requester contacts never appear in public discovery.

Ordinary drafts derive REQUESTER origin; scoped staff may create STAFF organizational drafts with private reachable requesting contact and separate creator/coordinator. Origin records provenance, not an extra publisher requirement.

features.title: Request moderation and state machine
acceptanceCriteria: Scoped staff can return, reject, publish, renew, fulfill, cancel, and expire due requests with reasons and audits.
Concurrent publication creates one public event; stale versions are rejected.

Publication requires approved coverage/response/contact/offer/slot policy, verified non-held hospital and reachable coordinator; closure/expiry stop coordination while a hospital hold preserves commitments and suspends pending timers.
Audited quantity/deadline/urgency edits reconcile slots, travelling donors and queued alerts; outside-app fulfillment, hold/release and corrected-outcome reopening resolve commitments safely.

Either authorized hospital staff or NSS coordinator can publish ready assigned REQUESTER or STAFF requests, including their creation; no mandatory second publisher. Scope/MFA/audit gates apply to both.

Only hospital staff set/release holds; preserve commitments/attendance, pause pending coordination timers, enforce effective request expiry and reschedule fresh work after release. Closed/held requests allow evidenced existing-visit reconciliation without new travel.

Only evidenced correction may reopen FULFILLED with fresh policy/deadline; other terminal requests require replacement. NORMAL/URGENT expand gradually and CRITICAL/EMERGENCY immediately use all coverage.

Assigned donation verification atomically fulfills/closes the request when required hospital-verified units are met, resolves surplus commitments and queues donor/requesting-person notifications plus dashboard updates.

features.title: Ownership, staffed hours, and escalation
acceptanceCriteria: Each submitted request has an owner, acknowledgement, backup, and partner-specific hours.
Overdue work escalates and outside-hours UI shows direct hospital contact.

features.title: Nearby request discovery
acceptanceCriteria: PostGIS search filters open verified requests by distance, group, urgency, and hospital.
Queries use bounded cursor pagination and manual-locality fallback.
Discovery defaults to 25 km with 10/25/50 km choices, independently of hospital-centred progressive alert zones.

features.title: Requester-safe timeline
acceptanceCriteria: Requester sees submission, acknowledgement, review, publication, coordination, and closure milestones.
No donor identity, check outcome, or hospital assessment appears.
Wider-area search and exhausted-search handoff appear only as neutral milestones, without donor identities, locations or check outcomes.

Requester timeline distinguishes confirmed donor coverage, shortfalls, donation verification pending and hospital-verified partial/complete units; coverage alone never claims fulfillment or tells the requester to abandon hospital advice.
Guarded admin notify-ready action tells the requesting person that required donors are confirmed/ready and extra donor searching can pause, with donation pending; later shortfalls notify them again.

features.title: Donor registration, profile and consent
acceptanceCriteria: Adult profile, group, locality, availability, contact/push consent, and alert pause work.
Withdrawal stops future matching/contact and stale preferences require reconfirmation.

Web/mobile onboarding records adult participation confirmation, name, self-reported group, Tamil/English preference, coarse locality, private callable E.164 number, availability and purpose-specific alert/contact consent, without collecting health answers at registration or test results.

Server activation gates block incomplete/unverified registration from matching and pledging; onboarding resumes idempotently without duplicate profiles or consent events and does not grant staff privileges.
Manual locality works with foreground location denied; denied OS push permission preserves registration and inbox access, separately from alert consent.

A valid private E.164 callable contactNumber is required for activation/pledging; numbers may be shared and remain self-reported until a coordinator call validates the contact version. Phone OTP/login identity remains F043.
Contact-sharing withdrawal immediately revokes number access, ends pre-donation commitments/releases slots and schedules neutral replacement work; manual handoff cannot delay it.

Alert withdrawal cancels waiting/offered commitments and donor push/matching; accepted commitments may continue with contact consent and inbox. OS push denial/availability pause alone does not cancel pledges.

features.title: Zone matching and all-coverage emergency alerts
acceptanceCriteria: Normal matching uses hospital-centred 10 km, additional >10-25 km, >25-50 km then all enabled Tamil Nadu service coverage; critical/emergency publication or upgrade immediately contacts all matching coverage.
Every stage respects group, activation, availability, consent, freshness and contact limits; no background movement tracking, nationwide broadcast or emergency consent override.

Empty stages advance immediately; approved urgency windows evaluate outstanding confirmed coverage. Full pending slots/offers pause only until bounded contact deadlines; waiting donors do not count as confirmed or donated units.

Shortfalls prioritize waiting replacements before wider invitations. Policy/coverage snapshots, search stage, due times and pause/exhaustion reasons persist; concurrent evaluation/retry/locality changes never repeat donor/request invitations.

Rejection suppresses repeat invitations; voluntary donor reopening remains possible while open. Closed/expired/fulfilled/held requests suppress queued actions; exhaustion notifies coordinator/backup with requester-safe manual handoff.

features.title: Pledge slots, waiting list and replacements
acceptanceCriteria: Donor can pledge/cancel; staff can coordinate and record no-show; only one active pledge exists.
Retries are idempotent and a pledge never counts as a completed donation.
Concurrent acceptance reserves only available slots and waitlists surplus by acceptance time then pledge ID; repeated taps/retries and competing coordinators cannot overbook.

Waiting/offered pledges count toward one active commitment. Withdrawal, contact timeout, decline, no-show and non-donation release capacity; promote one donor per vacant slot with a time-limited fresh response and coordinator check.

Contact/offer deadlines and replacement transitions are durable, versioned and idempotent; no waiting/offered donor gets travel instructions. Closure and quantity changes resolve affected commitments.

Hold suspends pending contact/offer timers without releasing slots; release rechecks permissions and reschedules fresh deadlines. Rejected/expired replacement ends that waiting commitment; renewed voluntary acceptance joins with a new queue time.

V1 slot capacity is max(0, requested units minus verified units); surplus donors wait rather than adding travel slots. Policy duration/freshness/contact-limit bounds and effective expiry caps follow plan.md.
Fresh replacement response reconfirms the pinned questionnaire and sharing consent before admin validation; waitlisted donors retain private submitted answers and receive waiting notices.

features.title: Donor checkbox questionnaire and admin validation call
acceptanceCriteria: After Accept, donor completes five default editable Yes/No/Unsure checkbox questions and explicit response-sharing consent; no preselected answers. Submission atomically creates reserved/waiting pledge and private versioned responses.
Assigned admins receive donor contact/details and submitted responses for validation; cross-donor/unassigned/public/requester reads and forged question versions are denied.

Authorized assigned hospital/NSS admins create/modify/activate immutable Tamil/English question versions under hospital-approved policy. Requests pin publication versions; existing answers remain unchanged.
Admin Call opens phone dialler as selected by owner; missing dialler handler provides clear phone-number fallback. Contact result, decision, reviewer/time/version are recorded; no call recording.

Successful call/contact-version validation plus proceed and live reservation are required for CONFIRMED; uncertain answers require hospital advice. Failed/unanswered calls time out neutrally; checkbox responses never declare clinical eligibility.
Changed phone invalidates old validation: pre-travel confirmation returns to pending check; attendance state remains while en-route/arrived donors are reconciled.

Approved private response storage/access/retention is tested; answers never enter push, broad socket events, requester/public views, analytics/logs/crash reports. Full hospital clinical screening remains separate.

features.title: Travel and arrival
acceptanceCriteria: Travel instructions require a proceed decision and donor may record en-route or arrival.
Offline retries, stale requests, and unsafe transitions cannot fabricate progress.

Cancellation, no-show, failed hospital visit and stale travel instructions notify staff and trigger safe replacement; holds/closure contact existing travellers and prevent further travel instructions.

features.title: Hospital final outcome
acceptanceCriteria: Either assigned partner role records donated, deferred, or did-not-donate with hospital proof.
Hospital controls clinical decision; duplicate, conflicting, or self-recorded outcomes are rejected.
Verified units alone count toward fulfillment; confirmed slots, pending proof and actual donated quantity are separate. No upload alone creates a donation.

Hospital non-donation releases capacity and notifies staff/replacement without clinical reasons; missing proof alone requires reconciliation rather than automatic replacement. Corrections/disputes and partial units remain auditable.

Verified donation atomically ends its commitment and reduces outstanding units/slot target before releasing capacity; it cannot promote an unnecessary replacement. Failure reasons are neutral operational codes without health free text.

Assigned hospital staff or NSS coordinator/admin validates donor-uploaded hospital certificate/evidence; verification reaching required units atomically closes and notifies affected donors/requesting person.

features.title: Private donation proof, verified history and certificates
acceptanceCriteria: Only evidenced donations create private history and optional shareable certificate.
Deferral/no-show creates none; revocation invalidates verification links.
Authorized donor presign, direct private R2 upload and idempotent completion follow the Xerox guide; default one readable JPEG/PNG/PDF per pledge, max 2 MiB after compression and five-minute grants.

Server verifies actual size/type/content, strips image metadata, quarantines suspicious files and flags reused proof for review. Cross-donor/unassigned access and public URLs are denied; receipt reference/named hospital attestation remains available.
Interrupted uploads retry safely; unfinalized objects clean up after 24 hours. Approved retention, private evidence backups and restoration preserve access; no medical reports are accepted.

features.title: Notification queue and worker
acceptanceCriteria: Inbox persists before push; FCM/APNs jobs retry, deduplicate, and expose failures.
Worker/provider outages do not lose committed events or send stale alerts.

Publication atomically queues normal Zone 1 or immediate all-coverage emergency matching; durable evaluation supports normal all-coverage fallback and bounded pending-slot pauses against confirmed coverage.

Crash/retry/concurrent evaluation preserves one stage event and one original invitation per donor/request; replacement offers have distinct deduplicated keys and device deliveries; state/consent/freshness/contact limits are rechecked before send.

Timed/empty-stage shortfalls, emergency upgrade, waiting promotion, contact/offer deadlines, exhausted handoff and closure/expiry/hold suppression pass integration tests; policy waiting is separate from processing latency.

PostgreSQL transactional outbox/job tables and a separate Node worker support leasing, due-time scheduling, retry/backoff and dead-letter visibility; API commits never depend on FCM/Socket.IO success.

Hold timer suspension/release, effective expiry and consent-withdrawal transactions survive restart without duplicate offers or stale calls/travel; withdrawal removes access before queued replacement work.

features.title: Device registration and inbox
acceptanceCriteria: Multiple devices, token rotation, logout cleanup, foreground display, and deep links work.
Denied push leaves usable inbox; deferral and requester notices reveal no health details.

Foreground accept/reject and background notification-tap journeys fetch live state; stale closure/offer notices cannot create acceptance or travel. Waiting, replacement and closure notices remain usable without push.

features.title: Public website
acceptanceCriteria: Purpose, verified directory, operating hours, help and privacy pages deploy with the Next.js App Router on Vercel; authenticated journeys use its server runtime.
Tamil/English responsive pages contain no embedded private data.

features.title: Requester and donor web journeys
acceptanceCriteria: Web account, request, discovery, pledge, timeline, outcome, and history use real API data.
Browser tests pass at phone/desktop sizes and cover loading, empty, error, offline states.
Tamil/English donor registration can resume, validate completion, use manual locality and continue with push denied; requester timeline shows safe wider-search/exhaustion milestones.
Next.js App Router, TanStack Query, Axios and HTTP-only server sessions connect to Express; generated TypeScript models and i18next copy match Flutter/OpenAPI contracts.

Web journeys cover accept/reject, waiting/replacement response, checkbox questionnaire with private admin-visible responses and compressed proof upload/verification-pending; requester distinguishes coordinated versus fulfilled units.

features.title: Staff dashboard
acceptanceCriteria: Scoped queues, assignment, basic check, outcome, evidence, audit, and administration work.
Both partner roles complete permitted journeys without direct database access.
Assigned staff see current alert zone, response counts, next evaluation and exhausted handoff; policy administration respects organizational scope and donor privacy.

Socket.IO room subscriptions and emissions require active session, staff MFA and hospital/NSS assignment; revocation disconnects clients and reconnect refetches REST state without duplicate transitions.
Zustand holds UI state only, Recharts reports remain scoped, and REST dashboard/inbox flows work during a socket outage.
Dashboard supports scoped click-to-call/contact attempts, reserved/confirmed/waiting counts, offer deadlines, failed-visit replacement, approved checklist editing and private uploaded-proof review.
Admin panel receives submitted questionnaire answers/details, opens phone dialler for validation and supports guarded donors-ready notices, certificate review and automatic verified-unit closure.

features.title: Flutter Android and iOS app
acceptanceCriteria: Flutter/Dart app with Riverpod, Dio, GoRouter, secure storage and Firebase Messaging supports registration/sign-in, profile, discovery, requests, pledges, travel, inbox and history.
Real-device journeys pass with denied location/push; no sample donation appears as real.
Tamil/English donor registration/activation, resume, manual locality, consent and denied push journeys use real server validation; wider-search/exhaustion milestones reveal no donor data.
Pinned Flutter/Dart builds pass analysis, unit/widget/integration tests and selected Maestro device flows; generated Dart API models and Tamil/English ARB copy match shared contracts.

Real-device journeys cover foreground accept/reject, background taps, waiting/replacement reconfirmation, checkbox questionnaire with private admin-visible responses, click-to-call and compressed proof upload with interrupted-network recovery.

features.title: Tamil and English completion
acceptanceCriteria: Core UI, errors, email, notifications, instructions, and help are translated and reviewed.
Native speakers review check/deferral copy and language switching preserves state.
Flutter localization/ARB and web/backend i18next preserve matching keys, placeholders, Tamil/English copy and notification meaning through automated parity checks.

features.title: Privacy requests and retention
acceptanceCriteria: Export/deletion, consent history, cleanup, backups, and approved legal holds follow a field-level schedule.
Withdrawal stops future contact; private exports and deletion are scoped and tested.

Field/object retention covers proof uploads and orphan cleanup; consent withdrawal suppresses queued promotion/contact. Questionnaire responses are private in storage/personal export and absent from public/shared export or telemetry.

Consent-withdrawal tests cover waiting/offered/confirmed/en-route/arrived pledges, immediate number-access removal and preserved attendance/evidence reconciliation; manual handoff never extends consent.
Private preliminary questionnaire response consent, withdrawal/access revocation, donor-only personal export, retention/deletion and audit are implemented without public/staff-bulk disclosure.

features.title: Abuse and support workflows
acceptanceCriteria: Fake/duplicate request reporting, support queue, and grievance route are auditable.
Tamil/English emergency guidance and support contacts are visible.

features.title: Security verification
acceptanceCriteria: ASVS-aligned tests cover RLS, MFA, CSRF, XSS, rate limits, secret exposure, and false confirmation.
No unresolved critical or high exploitable issue remains for pilot release.
Custom JWT/session replay, provider linking, trusted SQL actor context and Socket.IO room/revocation tests preserve the former authorization/privacy gates.
Upload authorization/content spoofing, private downloads, questionnaire version management, answer leakage and concurrent capacity/promotion tests pass with no self-verification.

features.title: Accessibility and responsive QA
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard, TalkBack, VoiceOver, contrast, large text, reduced motion, and 320-pixel layouts are tested.
Donor, requester, staff, and Tamil journeys have no blocking accessibility defect.

features.title: Resilience and performance QA
acceptanceCriteria: Slow/offline networks, concurrency, queue backlog, and measured pilot load are exercised.
Plan performance targets are measured and no unconfirmed mutation reports success.
Node worker restarts, socket disconnect/reconnect and database connection limits are tested; HTTP data remains authoritative during real-time delivery failures.
Concurrent two-slot acceptance, double promotion, contact/offer expiry, emergency escalation, outage recovery and delayed proof never overbook or falsely fulfill requests.

features.title: Monitoring and operational runbooks
acceptanceCriteria: Redacted logs, Sentry, uptime/queue/quota alerts, and incident procedures are live.
Operators rehearse outage, push failure, abuse, credential incident, bad release, and rollback.

features.title: Backup and restore
acceptanceCriteria: Encrypted R2 backups cover business data, backend identity/session data, Prisma migration history, SQL policies and configuration; restoration invalidates pre-restore sessions and preserves scoped access.
Restore succeeds before real enrollment and meets approved recovery targets.
Restoration covers required retained private proof objects and metadata, with reconciliation and scoped access; orphan cleanup and retention do not silently destroy verified evidence.

features.title: CI, staging, and deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Clean-checkout CI runs migrations, tests, scans, staging, deployment, and rollback.
Production and staging credentials/data are separate; release needs no undocumented steps.

CI separately checks Node/web and Flutter SDK/pub builds; Prisma migration deployment, Express/worker hosting on Railway/Render, Next.js on Vercel and managed PostGIS PostgreSQL have staging and rollback evidence.

features.title: Mobile release and provider setup
acceptanceCriteria: Production Firebase/APNs, SMTP, domains, signing, identifiers, and declarations are configured.
Real-device push/deep links pass and privacy declarations match actual collection.
Signed Flutter Android/iOS releases use non-secret API_URL configuration, native Firebase Messaging/APNs setup, supported deep links and platform-specific store/signing checks.

features.title: Partner approval and training
acceptanceCriteria: Hospitals/NSS sign off checklist, evidence, staffed hours, escalation, support, and backup contacts.
Both partner roles rehearse proceed, uncertainty, deferral, donation, outage, and dispute.

Partners approve versioned urgency response/contact/offer windows, slot targets, enabled coverage, immediate emergency broadcasts, checklist versions and upload retention; rehearse all-coverage exhaustion, waiting replacements, pending proof and coordinated-versus-fulfilled messaging.
Partners supply positive bounded policy values before publication; synthetic test policies are labelled and cannot silently become production defaults.

features.title: Controlled pilot launch
acceptanceCriteria: Invite agreed cohort and run supervised operations with quota and safety controls.
Real-data end-to-end journeys work and enrollment pauses when signed limits fail.

features.title: Pilot evaluation and corrections
acceptanceCriteria: Review response times, outcomes, no-shows, complaints, alerts, privacy, cost, and usability.
Observed defects are fixed/retested and partners sign expansion go/no-go.

features.title: Funded reliability and capacity
acceptanceCriteria: Upgrade database, backups, monitoring, and infrastructure from pilot measurements.
Load, restore, cost, alerts, and rollback evidence support larger cohort.

features.title: Phone identity and SMS
acceptanceCriteria: Funded OTP/SMS preserves accounts through identity linking and respects consent.
Sender/templates, rate limits, failures, and costs pass tests.
Phone OTP/SMS integrates through the Express identity-provider adapter and preserves backend account/session ownership; Supabase Auth is not required.

features.title: Tamil Nadu district rollout
acceptanceCriteria: Onboard additional verified partners and districts through configuration and training.
Every district has ownership, hospital evidence policy, support, access tests, and monitoring.

features.title: Final release and handoff
acceptanceCriteria: All planned features and release gates have evidence and named owners.
Technical/partner owners accept runbooks, restore proof, and ongoing review cadence.
